correctness.rationale: The two removed regions are disjoint 4-simplices of volume s^4/24. The polar is the hull of the cross-polytope and the tips ±(1,1,1,1)/(4−s); for s>0 each tip sees only its corresponding facet, giving two disjoint pyramids of volume s/[24(4−s)] each, with the formula also valid at s=0. The product gives D(s)=s/3+O(s²) and the recorded lower bound 2631s/8064; exact rational arithmetic confirms the three C=2 violations. For arbitrary fixed C>0 this lower bound beats the cubic as s tends to zero; C≤0 is immediate. The cube inclusions give 0≤δ≤−log(1−s/4)≤9s/32<D. Further, any Banach–Mazur sandwich B⊂TK_s⊂λB implies P(K_s)≤λ^4 P(B) by primal/polar inclusions and affine invariance. For x=D/P(B), δ≥x/[4(1+x)], and 0<x≤s/28≤1/56. Combining this with the lower bound on D gives δ≥(877/116736)s>s/140 throughout the interval, in particular at the checked nodes. Thus the quotient D/δ² is defined for s>0 and diverges. The side fallback is indeed false: the functional polar of exp(−|x|) is the indicator of [−1,1], so J=4 and variance 2 give a right side of 9/2. Inspected RESULT.md and artifacts/verify_target.py and verify_fallback_counterexample.py; independent simplex geometry and exact Fraction node evaluations, not reliance on archived statuses.
